clue.text: Made a silhouette look impressive

definitions.meaning: cutting a shape out of paper or card makes an outline picture
to make a striking appearance is an idiom using the same phrase

explanation.surface: Someone's shadow-portrait turned out to look rather striking.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, scissoring out a profile; idiomatically, presenting a striking appearance.

clue.text: Youngster first portrayed by Picasso, perhaps

parts.note: a cub is a young animal or a junior Scout
1ST, with the digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A child was the first subject painted by the Spanish master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'portrayed by' is linking padding; the crossword habit of reading the figure 1 as the letter I turns 1ST into IST.
explanation.definitionFit: Picasso co-founded Cubism, so he is an example of a painter of that movement.

clue.text: He assays an old coin

definitions.meaning: one who assays tries out or checks something
a former silver coin of Tudor times, later slang for a sixpence

explanation.surface: A metallurgist examines an antique piece of money.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tries things out; also the name of a Tudor shilling, later a sixpence.

clue.text: Was short of cash, so touched a man on board

definitions.meaning: an idiom for suffering from lack of money

definitions.text: so touched a man on board
definitions.meaning: read literally: put a hand on a piece in the board game of draughts (checkers)

explanation.surface: Being broke, someone tapped a fellow on a ship for a loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touched' suggests borrowing money and 'on board' a ship; actually it is a hand laid on a draughts piece. Draughts is the British name for checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means suffering financial hardship; literally it describes handling a checkers piece.

clue.text: Contact punter to make improvements

parts.note: to get someone is to reach them by phone
a punter is a gambler, one who places bets

explanation.surface: Ring up a gambler so that things improve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punter' is British for a gambler; 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover or progress is to improve, as a patient or a situation does.

clue.text: In Harare riots are less common

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: In Zimbabwe's capital, riots are not so frequent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something less common is scarcer, the comparative of an adjective for scarce.

clue.text: Continent, reflective fighting-fit, godly army

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the other way round, so the following pieces are read right to left

parts.note: A1 means in top condition, with the 1 read as the letter I
SA is the Salvation Army, a Christian organisation

explanation.surface: A list of a continent's virtues: introspective, fit, and devout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflective' turns A1 + SA back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of the world's landmasses.

clue.text: I always move around quietly and leave quietly

indicators.note: the letters are shifted about into a new order

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks about noiselessly and then exits unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move around' rearranges I ALWAYS together with P from the first 'quietly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart without fuss or notice, as from a party.

clue.text: Giving beer to a right-winger is dicey

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: Buying a drink for a Conservative is a risky business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving' and 'to' merely link. Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: From Latin for a gambler with dice: depending on chance.

clue.text: Have final authority to play pizzicato

definitions.meaning: an idiom for controlling events from behind the scenes
literally, plucking a violin's or cello's strings

explanation.surface: A musician directs things and plucks the violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically, secretly controlling people like puppets; literally, plucking rather than bowing an instrument.

clue.text: Bachelor gets French salt in Switzerland

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a place in that country

parts.note: BA is Bachelor of Arts
sel is the French word for salt

explanation.surface: A graduate seasons his food with salt while in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss city on the Rhine.

clue.text: A shade sour-quite strange

indicators.note: something strange is out of the ordinary, so these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A colour description: somewhat odd and sour.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenish-blue colour named after the gemstone.

clue.text: Lady takes articles to encase

parts.note: a female is she
the indefinite article is a
the definite article is the

explanation.surface: A woman collects items to pack in a case.
explanation.walkthrough: One word 'articles' supplies both the indefinite and definite articles.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a blade into its scabbard, enclosing it.

clue.text: Trusting high priest gripped by rage

indicators.note: one piece is held within the other, as something gripped is enclosed

parts.note: to rant is to rage loudly
Eli was the high priest in the Bible's Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A trusting cleric is seized by fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Depending on someone means having confidence in them.

clue.text: Unsettled when refused clearance to land

definitions.meaning: an aircraft denied permission to touch down stays aloft

explanation.surface: A pilot circles, unresolved, after the tower denies landing permission.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for undecided matters; literally, an aircraft still flying.

clue.text: Points to a man selling journals

definitions.note: describes a shopkeeper, so stands for a noun

parts.note: N, E, W and S are the compass points
a gent is a gentleman

explanation.surface: Directions given to a fellow who sells magazines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links; in Britain this shop sells papers, magazines and sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper who sells newspapers and magazines.

clue.text: Granted-Delaware is in agreement

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an accord is an agreement
DE is the postal abbreviation for the US state

explanation.surface: Permission granted: the state of Delaware has reached a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Given or bestowed, as an honour is conferred.

clue.text: Do sneers result in sanctions?

indicators.note: the letters produce a new word when reorganised, the word that results

explanation.surface: Asking whether mocking leads to penalties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sanctions' looks like penalties, but here it is the verb meaning approves.
explanation.definitionFit: To approve formally, as in giving official backing.

clue.text: On the other hand, criterion was invalid

indicators.note: something invalid is unsound, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: However, the standard used was found to be faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb for conversely or in the opposite way.

clue.text: The optic nerve is positioned near it

definitions.note: loosely, the light-sensitive part of the eye connected to that nerve

indicators.note: the letters are placed in a new position

explanation.surface: An anatomy fact: the nerve for seeing lies close to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose; the whole clue reads as a hint, since the optic nerve joins the eye at this layer.
explanation.definitionFit: The light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye, whose fibres form the optic nerve.

clue.text: A fragrance is rising

parts.note: a scent is a pleasant smell

explanation.surface: A perfume is wafting upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun sense: a climb or upward movement.

clue.text: Round and round and round

parts.note: the letter O is round in shape
rotund means plump or round

explanation.surface: A nonsense chant of the same word three times.
explanation.walkthrough: O plus ROTUND; the last 'round' describes a full, resonant voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing a voice or style that is full, sonorous and resonant.

clue.text: Old city outlined by the German painter

indicators.note: one piece forms the outline round the other

parts.note: der is a German word for the
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An ancient city is sketched by a German artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer, the German Renaissance artist and engraver.

clue.text: Stuffy injunction to vent fewer grievances

parts.note: an order to air, that is to express or ventilate
less, as in fewer complaints

explanation.surface: Telling a complainer to moan less makes the room close.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a command, the two words tell someone to air fewer grievances.
explanation.definitionFit: Without fresh ventilation, a room feels close.

clue.text: Release payment to the Stygian ferryman

definitions.meaning: to let go or set free
a fee for passage to Dis, the classical underworld across the Styx

explanation.surface: Freeing a soul after paying Charon to cross the Styx.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word: a charge for the trip to Dis, the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: To set free or let go; and split, a fare for passage to the classical underworld.

clue.text: One beset by smell and commotion

indicators.note: surrounded on all sides, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: nose means a smell, as of wine
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is surrounded by a stink and a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud din or racket.

clue.text: Hurry up and darn it!

explanation.surface: An impatient exclamation urging speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprint or rush; also a mild exclamation of frustration.

clue.text: He objects to patterns being changed

indicators.note: the letters are altered into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone opposes a change of designs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He objects' is also a nod to the religion's origin, the 1529 protest of German princes.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally one who protests; also a member of a Reformation church.
